_howto: Fuel how-to guides, one set per screen (help panel: "?" next to the profile, filter by Screen). Every guide starts by clicking its screen in the menu - that is how the Screen filter files it. Keys of the first 7 guides (vehicle, depot, price, delivery-*) are used by fueldashboard_tours.json (stepsFrom, skipSteps 2) and fueldashboard_setup.json - keep them and keep their first two steps (menu + open the form). Rebuilt 2026-10-16.

guides.title: Read the dashboard
guides.blurb: What every number and list on the Fuel dashboard means.

steps.title: Dashboard
steps.text: Open Dashboard in the menu on the left.

steps.title: This month
steps.text: Everything on the dashboard is for the month shown here, from the 1st until now. Click Refresh (or Sync Engine at the top) to load the latest fill-ups from the phones.

steps.title: Fill-ups, litres and fuel in tanks
steps.text: Fill-ups This Month counts every fill-up (all vehicles and depots). Litres Dispensed adds up their litres. Fuel In Tanks is what is in your own tanks right now. Road (outside) depots are not counted because their level is not tracked.

steps.title: Asset Utilisation and Operator Efficiency
steps.text: Asset Utilisation lists the litres each vehicle used this month. Operator Efficiency lists the litres per driver.

steps.title: Activity Distribution
steps.text: Litres per activity this month (what the fuel was used for), e.g. ploughing or transport.

steps.title: Fleet Efficiency
steps.text:
Each vehicle's latest efficiency: km per litre, or litres per hour for machines tracked in hours. You choose the units under Settings.

A number that looks impossible (e.g. 99999.9 km/L) almost always means an odometer was typed wrong. See the guide Find and fix an impossible efficiency.

steps.title: Physical Depot Inventory
steps.text: One tile per own tank with its level and capacity. Green is fine, amber is below 40% and red is below 15%. "No own tanks yet" means only road depots are registered.

guides.title: Find and fix an impossible efficiency
guides.blurb: A km/L like 99999 or 0.01 means a reading was typed wrong. Find the fill-up and correct it.

steps.title: Dashboard
steps.text: Open Dashboard in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Spot it
steps.text: Look for a vehicle whose efficiency is far too high or far too low. Efficiency is worked out from the distance between two odometer readings divided by the litres, so one wrong reading spoils it.

steps.title: Fueling Data
steps.text: Open Fueling Data in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Pick the vehicle
steps.text: Choose the vehicle. Then click the Date & Time heading to sort, and compare the Odometer column from fill-up to fill-up. The wrong one stands out (too high, too low, or an extra digit).

steps.title: Correct the reading
steps.text:
Click the pencil (Edit) on the wrong fill-up, fix the Odometer, and click Update Fill-up. If there was no reading, leave the odometer blank.

The vehicle's current reading and its km/L are worked out again from the fill-ups, and the change is written to the audit trail with your name.

steps.title: If the vehicle's reading itself is wrong
steps.text: On Vehicles, click the number in the Reading column to correct the vehicle's current odometer / hour meter (see Correct a vehicle's odometer or hour reading).

guides.title: Check the fill-ups for a day
guides.blurb: Look through one day's fill-ups with their photos, signature and GPS.

steps.title: Fuel Logs
steps.text: Open Fuel Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Choose the day
steps.text: With Period on One day, Fuel Logs shows one day at a time. Pick a date, or use the arrows either side to go a day back or forward.

steps.title: Period
steps.text: To see more than one day, choose This week, Last 7 days, This month, Last month or Custom range. From and To boxes then replace the day picker (change a date and it becomes a custom range). The footer shows the number of fill-ups and the litres for the period.

steps.title: The columns
steps.text:
Vehicle (and the depot / pump it came from), Driver, Used For (farm, unit, activity), Odometer, Photos, Signature, Nat. Road and Litres.

An amber Reason under the odometer means the driver typed a reason for an unusual reading. Hover over it to read it.

steps.title: Photos and signature
steps.text: Click a small photo to open it. The viewer shows which vehicle and when, with buttons to switch between the odometer, meter-before and meter-after photos of the same fill. Use Open Full Size for the original. The pin opens the place on Google Maps.

steps.title: Search in a column
steps.text: Type in the small box under a column heading to show only matching rows, e.g. a vehicle name or a driver. All the words you type must match.

steps.title: More rows
steps.text: A busy day spans several pages. Use Previous and Next.

guides.title: Capture a fill-up by hand
guides.blurb: Enter a fill-up that was not captured on the phone, e.g. from a paper slip.

steps.title: Fuel Logs
steps.text: Open Fuel Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Manual Entry
steps.text: Click Manual Entry. Nothing is saved until you click Save Fill-up, so it is safe to follow along.

steps.title: Date & time
steps.text: Required. When the fuel was dispensed. A date in the future is refused.

steps.title: Vehicle and driver
steps.text: Required. The vehicle or machine that got the fuel, and the driver / user who took it.

steps.title: Odometer
steps.text:
The odometer (or hour meter) at the fill. It is needed to work out km/L. It is required if Mandatory Odometer Capture is on under Settings.

With Typo Checks on, a reading lower than last time or a very big jump asks you to type a reason before it saves.

steps.title: Depot / pump
steps.text: Where the fuel came from. For your own tanks the tank level goes down by the litres. Choose a road depot for fuel bought at a filling station.

steps.title: Litres and pump meter
steps.text: Required: the litres dispensed. Type the Pump Meter Before and the After is worked out (before + litres), so the pump meter keeps adding up.

steps.title: Where it was used
steps.text: The Farm and Activity the fuel was used for. These drive the dashboard, the reports and the diesel rebate. Farming Department only shows when it is switched on under Settings.

steps.title: National road used
steps.text: Tick it if the vehicle drove on a public national road. That fuel is left out of the SARS diesel rebate claim.

steps.title: Save Fill-up
steps.text: Click Save Fill-up. It appears in Fuel Logs on its date, and the vehicle's reading and efficiency are updated.

guides.title: Correct a fill-up
guides.blurb: Change the vehicle, driver, odometer, litres, farm or activity of a captured fill-up.

steps.title: Fuel Logs
steps.text: Open Fuel Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Find it
steps.text: Go to the day of the fill-up, or choose a Period (e.g. This month) to see more days at once. Fueling Data also searches across all days.

steps.title: Edit
steps.text: Click the pencil on the fill-up's row.

steps.title: Vehicle & driver
steps.text: Change the Date & Time, Vehicle, Driver, Odometer (leave it blank if there was no reading) or Litres.

steps.title: Where it was used
steps.text: Change the Farm, Farm Unit, Activity or the National road used tick.

steps.title: A split fill-up
steps.text: If the fill-up was split over two activities, a Linked Split Part section shows. Changing this part's litres or % also changes the other part, so the two still add up to the total.

steps.title: Update Fill-up
steps.text: Click Update Fill-up. The change is written to the audit trail with your name. If you changed the odometer, the vehicle's reading and km/L are worked out again.

guides.title: Split one fill-up over two activities
guides.blurb: One tank of fuel used for two jobs - divide the litres between two activities.

steps.title: Fuel Logs
steps.text: Open Fuel Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Split
steps.text: Click the split button (the branch icon) on the fill-up's row.

steps.title: Part 1 (this fill)
steps.text: Choose the first activity, then its Litres or its %. The other box fills in by itself.

steps.title: Part 2 (new fill)
steps.text: Choose the second activity. Its litres are the rest, so the two parts always add up to the total shown at the top.

steps.title: Pump meter
steps.text: The pump meter readings stay on Part 1. Part 2 is a new linked fill-up with the same vehicle, driver and date.

steps.title: Confirm Split
steps.text: Click Confirm Split.

guides.title: Void (delete) a wrong fill-up
guides.blurb: Remove a duplicate or wrong fill-up. The litres go back to the tank.

steps.title: Fuel Logs
steps.text: Open Fuel Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Void
steps.text: Click the red bin on the fill-up's row.

steps.title: Type the reason
steps.text: A box asks why. The reason is required and is kept in the audit trail with your name.

steps.title: What happens
steps.text:
The fill-up is removed. Its litres go back into the tank, unless a tank reading was taken after it (then the reading stands). The vehicle's odometer and km/L are worked out again from the remaining fill-ups.

If only part of it is wrong, use Edit instead.

guides.title: Search all fill-ups (Fueling Data)
guides.blurb: Filter every fill-up by vehicle, activity or department, sort and search.

steps.title: Fueling Data
steps.text: Open Fueling Data in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Narrow the list by Vehicle, Activity and Department. The list changes as you choose.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Type a driver, farm or depot name to find matching fill-ups.

steps.title: Sort and column search
steps.text: Click a heading (Date, Vehicle, Driver, Odometer, Litres...) to sort by it. Click again to reverse. The boxes under the headings search in that column only.

steps.title: Fix a fill-up from here
steps.text: Each row has the same buttons as Fuel Logs: the pencil to Edit, the branch to Split and the red bin to Void.

steps.title: Manual Entry (Split)
steps.text: Opens the same Manual Fuel Entry form as on Fuel Logs. See Capture a fill-up by hand.

guides.title: Check the trips for a day
guides.blurb: See the trips drivers logged: client, destination, pallets, temperature and evidence.

steps.title: Trip Logs
steps.text: Open Trip Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Choose the day
steps.text: With Period on One day: one day at a time. Pick a date or use the arrows.

steps.title: Period
steps.text: Choose This week, Last 7 days, This month, Last month or Custom range to see the trips of a longer period. From and To boxes replace the day picker.

steps.title: The columns
steps.text: Driver & Vehicle, Client & Destination, the trip Activity, Units Delivered (pallets), Odometer & Temp (load temperature), Location (opens the GPS point on a map) and Evidence (photos and signature, click to open).

steps.title: Search and pages
steps.text: Type in the boxes under the headings to search a column. Use Previous / Next for more rows.

guides.title: Capture a trip by hand
guides.blurb: Enter a trip that was not logged on the phone.

steps.title: Trip Logs
steps.text: Open Trip Logs in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Manual Entry
steps.text: Click Manual Entry. Nothing is saved until you click Save Trip.

steps.title: Trip
steps.text: Required: Date & Time, Vehicle and Driver / User. Then the Trip Activity (set up under Management > Trip Activities), the Client and the Destination (stop).

steps.title: Readings
steps.text: The Odometer at the stop, the Units Delivered (pallets) and the load Temperature (Cold, Medium, Slightly High, High).

steps.title: Save Trip
steps.text: Click Save Trip.

guides.title: Plan a delivery or collection
guides.blurb: Load a stop for the drivers: client, destination, date and what is being delivered.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.text: You need the client (Management > Clients) and your products and units (Management > Deliveries). A line can also be free text.

steps.title: New Delivery
steps.text: Click New Delivery. Nothing is saved until Save Delivery.

steps.title: Type
steps.text: Delivery: goods go to the client. Collection: goods come back from the client.

steps.title: Client and reference
steps.text: Required: the Client. Your Reference is your invoice or order number. It prints on the ePOD.

steps.title: Where and when
steps.text: The Destination (farm, depot or address) and the Planned Date.

steps.title: Driver and vehicle
steps.text: Optional. A delivery with no driver is shown to every driver, and the first one to take it "claims" it. Pick a driver to give it to one person.

steps.title: Notes for the driver
steps.text: Anything the driver must know, e.g. "Call before arriving".

steps.title: What is being delivered
steps.text: Click Add Line for each item: choose the product (or free text), a description, the quantity and the unit. Leave a line empty to remove it.

steps.title: Save Delivery
steps.text: Click Save Delivery. It gets a number and shows on the drivers' phones as Pending.

guides.title: Find a delivery and see what happened
guides.blurb: Filter deliveries, read the statuses and open a stop's details.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Set From / To, the Status, Client or Driver, or search a number, reference or place. Tick Exceptions only to see only stops with a problem. Then click Filter.

steps.title: Statuses
steps.text:
Pending: not done yet. Delivered: everything delivered. Partial: less than planned (waits in Resolve). Failed: could not be done (the driver picked a reason). Cancelled: cancelled in the office.

The Driver column shows who it was given to, Claimed by someone, or Open to all.

steps.title: Open
steps.text: Click the eye on a row to see the stop: lines planned and delivered, notes, photos, signatures and GPS.

guides.title: Change or cancel a delivery
guides.blurb: Edit a stop before the driver does it, or cancel it.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Edit
steps.text: The pencil only shows while a delivery is Pending. Click it to change the client, date, driver or lines, then Save Delivery.

steps.title: Cancel
steps.text: Click the red Cancel button on the row. A delivered stop cannot be cancelled. Use Collect back to bring goods back instead.

steps.title: Your deliveries
steps.text: The buttons on each row change with the status: open, edit (Pending), collect back (Delivered / Partial), ePOD and email (done stops) and cancel.

guides.title: Resolve a partial or failed stop
guides.blurb: Decide what happens to goods that were not delivered: a follow-up stop or close it.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.text: Click the Resolve tab.

steps.title: Waiting to be resolved
steps.text: Every Partial or Failed stop waits here with what was planned, delivered and is outstanding. The number on the tab is how many are waiting.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.text: Click Resolve on a stop.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.text: For a new stop: the Follow-up Date, a Driver (optional) and a Note (why, or what was agreed with the client).

steps.title: Create Follow-up or Close As Is
steps.text: Create Follow-up makes a new Pending stop for the outstanding goods. Close As Is accepts what happened, and nothing more is delivered.

guides.title: Collect goods back
guides.blurb: Create a collection (COL-) linked to a delivery, e.g. returns or empty crates.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Collect back
steps.text: Click the Collect back button (circular arrow) on a Delivered or Partial delivery.

steps.title: What to collect
steps.text: Leave the lines as they are to collect everything that was delivered, or lower the quantities. Then the Planned Date and a Driver (optional).

steps.title: Create Collection
steps.text: Click Create Collection. It is listed on the Collections tab and on the drivers' phones.

guides.title: Send or resend an ePOD
guides.blurb: Open the ePOD PDF, email it to the client and check what was sent.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Open Deliveries in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Open the ePOD
steps.text: On a Delivered, Partial or Failed stop, click the PDF button to open the ePOD (lines, signatures and, if switched on, photos).

steps.title: Email it
steps.text: Click the amber envelope to email the ePOD to the client's ePOD email (set under Management > Clients > Contact). With Email The ePOD Automatically on (Settings), it is sent by itself as soon as the stop syncs.

steps.title: ePOD Emails
steps.text: Click the ePOD Emails tab.

steps.title: What was sent
steps.text: Every ePOD email: when, to whom (and CC), whether it was automatic or by hand, and the Result. A failed one shows why, e.g. no email address on the client.

guides.title: Add a vehicle or asset
guides.blurb: Register a vehicle, tractor or machine with its reading, licence and service interval.

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Add Vehicle
steps.text: Click Add Vehicle. Nothing is saved until Save Vehicle.

steps.title: Name and asset tag
steps.text: Required: a Name / Registration the drivers recognise. The Asset Tag (QR) is optional. It is the code drivers scan on the phone to pick this vehicle.

steps.title: Type and tracking
steps.text: What it is (Truck, Tractor, Bakkie, Generator, Heavy Machinery, or Sub-Contractor Asset, which asks which sub-contractor). Tracking: Kilometres for road vehicles, Machine Hours for tractors and machines.

steps.title: Make & model and fleet number
steps.text: Optional, for your records and reports.

steps.title: Current reading
steps.text: Required: the odometer or hour meter now. The next fill-up's reading is checked against it, and efficiency starts from it.

steps.title: Licence and service
steps.text: Licence Expiry feeds the Licence Audit. Last Service and Service Interval (km or hours) work out when the next service is due.

steps.title: Save Vehicle
steps.text: Click Save Vehicle. It appears in the register and on the phones.

guides.title: Find and edit a vehicle
guides.blurb: Search the register and change a vehicle's name, tag, type, service or licence date.

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Find it
steps.text: Type a name or tag, or choose a Vehicle Type. Click a column heading to sort by it.

steps.title: Edit on the row
steps.text:
The name, tag, type, service and licence date are boxes you can type in straight on the row. Change what you need, then click the green save button on that row.

Changing Tracks KM / Tracks HRS saves straight away.

steps.title: Efficiency column
steps.text: The latest km/L (or L/hr) of the vehicle, in the units chosen under Settings. Pending... means there are not yet two fill-ups with readings.

guides.title: Correct a vehicle's odometer or hour reading
guides.blurb: Fix the vehicle's current reading when it is wrong (e.g. after a new odometer).

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Reading
steps.text: Click the number in the Reading column of the vehicle.

steps.title: Type the new reading
steps.text:
Type the correct reading and click OK. The change is audited with your name and the old and new readings. It affects efficiency, so only change it when the vehicle's reading is really wrong.

If one fill-up has the wrong reading, correct that fill-up instead (Fuel Logs > Edit). The vehicle reading is then worked out again by itself.

guides.title: Track services and mark a vehicle serviced
guides.blurb: Set the service interval, see what is due and record a service.

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Service (Last | Interval)
steps.text: On each row: the reading at the last service and the interval (every so many km or hours). Under them: Next at, an amber Due in (within 10% of the interval) or a red Overdue by.

steps.title: Mark as serviced
steps.text: After a service click the wrench on the row. The last service becomes the current reading, and the next one is due one interval later. An interval must be filled in first.

steps.title: Service Audit
steps.text: Click Service Audit for a list of every vehicle's service status. It opens below the register, with Export CSV.

guides.title: Check licence expiry dates (Licence Audit)
guides.blurb: See which vehicle licences have expired or expire soon, and export the list.

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Licence Expiry column
steps.text: Each vehicle's licence date, with Valid, an amber number of days left (30 days or less) or a red Expired. Change the date on the row and click save.

steps.title: Licence Audit
steps.text: Click Licence Audit.

steps.title: Compliance & Service Report
steps.text: Every vehicle with its licence status. Export CSV downloads it, and the X closes it.

guides.title: Stop using a vehicle, or bring it back
guides.blurb: Take a sold or scrapped vehicle off the lists at month end, or restore it.

steps.title: Vehicles
steps.text: Open Vehicles in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Stop at month end
steps.text: Click the red ban button on the vehicle's row and confirm. It stays usable until the last day of this month (so this month's fill-ups and reports stay complete), then it is taken off the lists and the phones. The row shows a red Ends date.

steps.title: Restore
steps.text: Changed your mind? Click Restore on that row before or after the date. Its history is never deleted.

guides.title: Register a driver
guides.blurb: Add a driver with licence details and link them to their phone login.

steps.title: Drivers
steps.text: Open Drivers in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Add New Driver
steps.text: Click Add New Driver (top right). Nothing is saved until Register Driver.

steps.title: Driver
steps.text: Required: the Full Name. The ID Number is optional.

steps.title: Licence
steps.text: The Licence No., its Code (e.g. EC1, C1), the Licence Expiry and the PDP Expiry (professional driving permit). Expiry dates show as warnings on the roster.

steps.title: Link to Mobile User
steps.text: Choose the user this driver logs in to the phone app as. Then every fill-up that user captures counts as this driver in the reports.

steps.title: Register Driver
steps.text: Click Register Driver. The pop-up closes and the driver appears in the Driver Roster.

guides.title: Edit a driver, or deactivate one
guides.blurb: Change details, link a phone user, or hide a driver who left.

steps.title: Drivers
steps.text: Open Drivers in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Driver Roster
steps.text: Every driver with their ID number, licence number and code, licence and PDP expiry, linked phone user and status.

steps.title: Edit
steps.text: Click the pencil (Edit) on the driver row.

steps.title: Edit Driver
steps.text: Change the name, ID number, licence details or the linked mobile user, then click Save Driver.

steps.title: Deactivate or restore
steps.text: The red ban on a row hides the driver from all lists and the phone app. Their history stays. Restore on an inactive driver brings them back.

guides.title: Register a depot and its pumps
guides.blurb: Add a tank (or a road filling station) with its capacity and pumps.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Add Depot / Tank
steps.text: Click Add Depot / Tank. Nothing is saved until Save Depot & Pumps.

steps.title: Tank details
steps.text: Required: the Depot / Tank Name and the Capacity in litres. Also the Location and the Fuel Type.

steps.title: External / road depot
steps.text: Tick it for a public filling station. There is then no tank level or pump meter to track. Fill-ups just record where the fuel was bought.

steps.title: Meter resets to zero
steps.text: Tick it for a meter that is set back to 0 for every fill, e.g. a jerry can. The app then starts at 0 each time and does not flag a meter gap.

steps.title: Add Pump
steps.text: Click Add Pump for each pump (fuelling point) on this tank: its name, the QR Tag drivers scan, and the Starting Meter reading.

steps.title: Save Depot & Pumps
steps.text: Click Save Depot & Pumps. Then record the fuel in the tank with Refill or Tank Reading.

guides.title: Record fuel delivered into a tank (refill)
guides.blurb: Add a fuel supplier delivery to a tank so the level is right.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Refill
steps.text: Click Refill on the tank's row.

steps.title: Add New Refill
steps.text: Required: the Refill Date and the Litres Added. The PO Number / Ref is your order or delivery note number.

steps.title: Save Refill
steps.text: Click Save Refill. The tank level goes up by the litres.

steps.title: Refill History
steps.text: Every refill of this tank. The red bin deletes a wrong refill and takes its litres back out of the tank.

guides.title: Enter a dip reading or correct a tank level
guides.blurb: Set the tank to what you measured, or let the system work it out from the logs.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Tank Level
steps.text: The bar shows the level the system worked out: refills in, fill-ups and transfers out. Green is fine, amber is below 40% and red is below 15% (or below zero, which means something was missed).

steps.title: Tank Reading
steps.text: Click Tank Reading on the tank's row.

steps.title: Measured level
steps.text: The Reading Date and the True Level in litres (e.g. from a dipstick). Saving replaces the worked-out level from that moment.

steps.title: Work out the level from the logs
steps.text: Not sure? Click this to see the sum: the last reading, plus refills and transfers in, minus fill-ups and transfers out. Save Worked Out Level uses it. It is written to the audit trail.

guides.title: Move fuel from one tank to another
guides.blurb: Record a transfer so both tank levels stay right.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.text: Click Transfer on the tank the fuel comes from.

steps.title: To Tank and litres
steps.text: Required: the Transfer Date, the tank it goes To and the Litres. Notes are optional (reason or PO).

steps.title: Confirm Transfer
steps.text: Click Confirm Transfer. One tank goes down and the other goes up by the litres.

guides.title: Manage pumps, QR tags and meter readings
guides.blurb: Add or remove pumps, change their QR tag, or correct a pump meter.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Pumps
steps.text: Click the pump button on the depot's row.

steps.title: Pumps
steps.text: Each pump's name, QR tag (what drivers scan) and meter reading. Change them on the row and click the green save. A new meter reading asks you to confirm and is audited with your name. Road depots have no meter.

steps.title: Add or remove
steps.text: Add Pump adds another fuelling point. The red bin removes a pump (its past fill-ups stay).

guides.title: Edit a depot's details, or deactivate it
guides.blurb: Rename, move, resize or retire a depot.

steps.title: Fuel Depots
steps.text: Open Fuel Depots in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Manage depot
steps.text: Click the Manage button (sliders) on the depot's row.

steps.title: Details & Capacity
steps.text: Change the name, location, capacity or the meter resets to zero tick, then click Save Details.

steps.title: Actions
steps.text: The same Manage Pumps, Refill, Tank Reading and Transfer as on the row.

steps.title: Deactivate Depot
steps.text: Takes the depot off the lists and the phones. Its history and reports stay.

guides.title: Link a warehouse to Fuel (Inventory)
guides.blurb: Inventory needs one warehouse assigned to the Fuel module first.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: Open Inventory in the menu on the left.

steps.title: No warehouse assigned?
steps.text: If the screen says No Warehouse Assigned To Fuel, open the Assets module, go to Warehouses, and click Assign to Fuel on the warehouse that belongs to Fuel. It must be a Storage warehouse (not Consumption), and only one can be assigned.

steps.title: Check Again
steps.text: Come back here and click Check Again (or Refresh). The warehouse name then shows at the top of Warehouse Inventory.

guides.title: Receive stock (oil, filters, parts)
guides.blurb: Book stock into the Fuel warehouse when it arrives.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: Open Inventory in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Receive Stock
steps.text: Click Receive Stock.

steps.title: Reference
steps.text: The delivery note or PO number. It shows in the stock history.

steps.title: Item
steps.text: Required. Only items counted by quantity are listed. Not in the list? Click New Item next to it (see Create a new stock item).

steps.title: Quantity Received
steps.text: Required. How many came in.

steps.title: Receive Stock
steps.text: Click Receive Stock. The quantity on hand goes up, and the receipt is listed on the Stock In / Out History tab with your name.

guides.title: Take stock out
guides.blurb: Book stock out when it is used or issued to someone.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: Open Inventory in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Take Stock Out
steps.text: Click Take Stock Out.

steps.title: Item and quantity
steps.text: Required: the Item and the Quantity To Take Out. What is available shows under the quantity. You cannot take out more than there is.

steps.title: Reason / Taken By
steps.text: Required. What it is for and who took it, e.g. "Issued to workshop - J. Dlamini".

steps.title: Take Out
steps.text: Click Take Out. It shows on the Stock In / Out History tab with the reason and your name.

guides.title: Create a new stock item
guides.blurb: Add an item (counted by quantity) to the stock list.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.text: Open Inventory in the menu on the left.

steps.title: New Item
steps.text: Click New Item.

steps.title: Item Name
steps.text: Required, e.g. "Hydraulic Oil 20L".

steps.title: Item Code
steps.text: Required and unique across the whole system. Click Generate for a code.

steps.title: Category and description
steps.text: Optional. Pick an existing category or type a new one.

steps.title: Create Item
steps.text: Click Create Item. Serialised items (with serial numbers) are created in the Assets module instead.

guides.title: Add farms and field units (with map boundaries)
guides.blurb: The farms and units fuel is used on, with a map area for the heat map and phone GPS.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Farms & Units
steps.text: Click the Farms & Units tab.

steps.title: Add Parent Farm
steps.text: Type the farm name. Click the pin to set its map boundary (optional but needed for the heat map), then Add.

steps.title: Set a map boundary
steps.text: In the map window: search a place, set the Radius in metres, click the map to place the boundary (drag the pin to move it) and click Confirm Location. The badge then changes from Not Set to set.

steps.title: Add Field Unit
steps.text: Choose the farm, type the unit name and its size in hectares, set the pin if you like, and click Add.

steps.title: Change them later
steps.text: Farms and their units are listed below. Edit a name or size on the row and click the green save. An amber pin means there is no map boundary yet. Click it to set one.

guides.title: Add fuel activities and the diesel rebate
guides.blurb: What fuel is used for, and which activities can claim the SARS diesel rebate.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Activities
steps.text: Click the Activities tab.

steps.title: Add an activity
steps.text: Type the activity, e.g. "Silage Harvesting".

steps.title: Can claim the diesel rebate
steps.text: Tick it if fuel for this activity qualifies for the diesel rebate (on-farm primary production). Untick it for activities that do not, e.g. private or office use. The SARS logbook report uses this.

steps.title: Add
steps.text: Click Add.

steps.title: Change them later
steps.text: Rename or change the rebate tick on a line and click the green save. The red ban stops using an activity. Past fill-ups keep it.

guides.title: Add farming departments
guides.blurb: Optional extra grouping of fuel, e.g. by division.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Farming Depts
steps.text: Click the Farming Depts tab.

steps.title: Add a department
steps.text: Type the name, e.g. "Avocado Division", and click Add. The red ban on a line stops using it.

steps.title: Switch it on
steps.text: The department field only shows on Manual Entry and the phone when Farming Department Tracking is on under Settings.

guides.title: Add trip activities
guides.blurb: The trip types drivers choose when they log a trip.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Trip Activities
steps.text: Click the Trip Activities tab.

steps.title: Add a trip activity
steps.text: Type it, e.g. "Delivery Run", and click Add. The red ban on a line stops using it.

guides.title: Add delivery clients and their ePOD email
guides.blurb: Clients for deliveries and trips, with who gets the ePOD and their delivery history.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Clients
steps.text: Click the Clients tab.

steps.title: Add a client
steps.text: Type the client name and click Add.

steps.title: Contact and History
steps.text: Contact: the Email for ePODs, contact person and phone, and a tick for Do not email ePODs to this client. History: every delivery to this client with its ePOD.

guides.title: Add sub-contractors and their vehicles
guides.blurb: Track fuel given to contractors' vehicles separately.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Sub-Contractors
steps.text: Click the Sub-Contractors tab.

steps.title: Add a sub-contractor
steps.text: Type the name and click Add.

steps.title: Link their vehicles
steps.text: On Vehicles > Add Vehicle, choose the type Sub-Contractor Asset and pick the sub-contractor. Their fuel then shows on the By Sub-Contractor report.

guides.title: Set the fuel price
guides.blurb: The price per litre from a date, so every fill-up is costed. Back-dating is allowed.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Fuel Pricing
steps.text: Click the Fuel Pricing tab.

steps.title: Fuel Type
steps.text: Diesel 50ppm, Diesel 500ppm, Petrol 95, Petrol 93 or Paraffin.

steps.title: Price per Litre and Valid From
steps.text:
The price in Rand, and the date it applies from. A fill-up is costed when it is captured, at the price valid on its date for its depot's fuel type.

A back-dated price is used for fill-ups captured later for those dates (manual entries, phones syncing late). Fill-ups already saved keep their cost.

steps.title: Save Price
steps.text: Click Save Price.

steps.title: Price History and trends
steps.text: Every price you entered (the bin removes a wrong one). The Pricing Trends chart on the right shows prices over the dates you choose.

guides.title: Set up delivery products, units and fail reasons
guides.blurb: The lists the New Delivery form and the drivers pick from.

steps.title: Management
steps.text: Open Management in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Deliveries
steps.text: Click the Deliveries tab.

steps.title: Units of Measure
steps.text: Add units first: a short code (e.g. CRATE) and a name (Crate), then Add Unit.

steps.title: Delivery Products
steps.text: The product name, an optional code and its default unit, then Add.

steps.title: Failed Delivery Reasons
steps.text: The reasons a driver can pick when a stop cannot be completed, e.g. "Gate locked". Click Add.

steps.title: Removing
steps.text: The red ban on a line stops using it. Deliveries that already use it keep it (marked inactive).

guides.title: Run a report and export it
guides.blurb: Choose a report, set its filters, read the summary cards and export to Excel or PDF.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Open Reports in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Report
steps.text: Choose the report (see Which report do I need?). It shows straight away for this month; a line under it says what the report contains.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Click Filters. It opens the filters of the report you chose.

steps.title: Dates (and driver / vehicle)
steps.text: The Start Date and End Date. Some reports also ask for a Driver or a Vehicle here. The evidence and pallet reports are for one driver on one day. Click Apply Filters; Reset goes back to this month.

steps.title: Cards and table
steps.text: The cards sum up what the report shows (e.g. fill-ups, litres, vehicles, drivers). Click a column heading to sort (again for the other way), and type in the box under a heading to search that column.

steps.title: Export
steps.text: Export downloads the report in Excel. The evidence reports give a PDF with the photos and signatures instead. Refresh loads it again with the latest fill-ups.

guides.title: Which report do I need?
guides.blurb: What each report shows.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Open Reports in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Fuel reports
steps.text: Global Transaction Report: every fill-up in the dates. Fuel Efficiency Report: km/L or L/hr per fill-up and the average. By Driver / By Vehicle (Detailed): every fill-up for a driver or vehicle. By Activity / By Sub-Contractor (Summary): totals per activity or contractor.

steps.title: Proof and finance
steps.text: Fuel Evidence Report: a PDF of one driver's fill-ups for a day with photos and signatures. Accountant Fuel Sheet: fill-ups for your bookkeeper with registration, depot / pump, litres, meter and odometer. SARS Diesel Rebate Logbook: the logbook for the diesel rebate claim.

steps.title: Trips and fleet
steps.text: Trip Log Report: trips in the dates (one vehicle or all). Trip Evidence Report: a PDF of a driver's trips for a day with evidence. Stop & Pallet Log Sheet: a driver's stops and pallets for a day. Vehicle Service Report: service status of the fleet.

guides.title: Produce the SARS diesel rebate logbook
guides.blurb: The logbook for your diesel rebate claim, and what makes it correct.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Open Reports in the menu on the left.

steps.title: What it needs
steps.text: The logbook is only as good as the fill-ups: an odometer / hour reading on each fill, the right activity (with Can claim the diesel rebate ticked under Management > Activities) and the National road used tick for road use, which does not qualify.

steps.title: Choose the report
steps.text: Choose SARS Diesel Rebate Logbook. The cards show the litres and the qualifying litres.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Click Filters. It opens the filters of the report you chose.

steps.title: The claim period
steps.text: Set the start and end of the period you are claiming for, then click Apply Filters.

steps.title: Export
steps.text: Check the report, then click Export for the full logbook in Excel (qualifying and non-qualifying litres) for your records or your tax practitioner.

guides.title: Email a report automatically
guides.blurb: Have a report emailed every day, week or month.

steps.title: Reports
steps.text: Open Reports in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Scheduled Mailers
steps.text: Click Scheduled Mailers (top right).

steps.title: Report and frequency
steps.text: The Report (Global, Driver, Vehicle or Trip Log) and how often: Daily (6 AM), Weekly (Monday) or Monthly (the 1st).

steps.title: Data Range
steps.text: What it covers: Yesterday, Last Week or Last Month.

steps.title: Email To
steps.text: One or more addresses, comma separated. They must be your own users, or on a domain allowed under Settings > Report Emails (e.g. your accountants).

steps.title: Save and test
steps.text: Click Save. Test sends it right now so you can check it arrives.

steps.title: Your schedules
steps.text: Each schedule with its Next Run. The pencil edits it and the bin removes it.

guides.title: Choose what the phone must capture
guides.blurb: The fuel switches: odometer, photos, typo checks, national road, departments and efficiency units.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Switches save straight away
steps.text: Every switch on this screen saves as soon as you click it, for the whole company (web and phones).

steps.title: Mandatory Odometer Capture
steps.text: On: a fill-up cannot be saved without an odometer / hour reading. Recommended, because efficiency and the SARS logbook need it.

steps.title: Mandatory Phone Photos
steps.text: On: the phone requires the odometer, meter-before and meter-after photos.

steps.title: Typo Checks (Ask for a Reason)
steps.text: On: more litres than the tank holds, an odometer lower than last time, or a very big jump must be explained before saving. Off: nothing is asked, but the phone still refuses a lower odometer. Future dates are always refused.

steps.title: National road
steps.text: Show National Road on the Phone: off hides the question (saved as No). Default National Road Policy: on starts it ticked for new entries.

steps.title: Farming Department Tracking
steps.text: Adds the optional department field to Manual Entry and the phone.

steps.title: Efficiency display
steps.text: Show KM vehicles as km/L or L/km, and machines as L/hr or hrs/L.

steps.title: Allowed Report Domains
steps.text: Scheduled reports can go to your own users plus these domains (comma separated). Click Save next to it.

guides.title: Set the delivery and ePOD rules
guides.blurb: What drivers must capture at a stop, and how ePODs are emailed.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: What the driver must capture
steps.text: Mandatory Evidence Photo, POD Photo, Client Signature and Driver Signature. Damaged Goods Need A Photo forces a note and photo for damaged lines.

steps.title: What drivers may do
steps.text: Allow Partial Deliveries: less than planned becomes Partial and waits in Resolve. Allow Unplanned Stops: drivers may capture a stop that was never loaded.

steps.title: ePOD emails
steps.text: Email The ePOD Automatically as soon as a stop syncs. ePOD For Failed Stops, Photos On The ePOD, and an Office Copy For Opted-Out Clients.

steps.title: Vehicle, loading point and CC
steps.text: How the vehicle on the ePOD is chosen, the Default Loading Point, and an office address to CC on every ePOD.

guides.title: Find a setting quickly
guides.blurb: Search Settings, or show only the settings that change the phone app.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Search settings
steps.text: Type a word such as photo, odometer or ePOD, then pick a result. Settings jumps to it and the setting flashes so you can spot it. Press / anywhere in Settings to come back to this box.

steps.title: Only the phone app
steps.text: Tick this to dim every setting that does not change what drivers see on their phones. Untick it to see all settings again.

steps.title: Changes save straight away
steps.text: Each switch saves the moment you click it, for the whole company, on the web and on every phone. The only Save button is next to Allowed Report Domains.

guides.title: Make every fill-up come with proof
guides.blurb: Require an odometer reading and photos before a fill-up can be saved.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Require the odometer
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory Odometer Capture. A fill-up can then only be saved with an odometer or hour reading. Fuel efficiency and the SARS logbook both need this reading.

steps.title: Require the photos
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory Phone Photos. The phone then asks for a photo of the odometer, and of the pump meter before and after filling.

steps.title: Checking the proof
steps.text: The photos show as small thumbnails on each row in Fuel Logs. Click one to see it full size.

guides.title: Catch typing mistakes on fill-ups
guides.blurb: Ask drivers for a reason when the litres or the odometer look wrong.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Switch on Typo Checks
steps.text: Switch on Typo Checks (Ask for a Reason). The phone then asks for a typed reason when the litres are more than the tank holds, the odometer is lower than last time, or the odometer jumps a lot.

steps.title: Where the reasons show
steps.text: A fill-up with a reason gets an amber Reason badge next to its odometer in Fuel Logs. Hover over the badge to read what the driver typed.

steps.title: If you switch it off
steps.text: Nothing is asked any more. The phone still refuses an odometer lower than the last one, and dates in the future are always refused.

guides.title: Set up national road use for the diesel rebate
guides.blurb: Decide whether drivers are asked about public road use, and what the default answer is.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Ask the drivers
steps.text: Switch on Show National Road on the Phone if drivers should say whether the fuel was used on a public national road. Fuel used on national roads is left out of the SARS diesel rebate.

steps.title: Choose the usual answer
steps.text: Switch on Default National Road Policy if most of your fuel is used on public roads. New fill-ups then start with National Road Used ticked, and drivers untick it for farm work. Leave it off if most fuel is used on the farm.

steps.title: If you hide the question
steps.text: With Show National Road on the Phone off, the phone saves every fill-up as No. You can still change a fill-up later on Manual Entry or Edit.

guides.title: Track fuel by farming department
guides.blurb: Add a department field to fill-ups, for example one per division.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Switch on departments
steps.text: Switch on Farming Department Tracking. Manual Entry and the phone fuel form then show an optional department field.

steps.title: Add the departments
steps.text: Next, add your departments under Management > Farming Depts. The guide Add farming departments walks you through it.

guides.title: Show fuel efficiency the way your managers read it
guides.blurb: Choose km/L or L/km for vehicles, and L/hr or hrs/L for machines.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Vehicles on kilometres
steps.text: Pick Km / Litre to show how far a vehicle goes on one litre, for example 10 km/L. Pick Litres / Km to show the fuel used per kilometre, for example 0.1 L/km.

steps.title: Machines on hours
steps.text: Pick Litres / Hour for the usual tractor figure, for example 15 L/hr. Pick Hours / Litre to show how long one litre lasts, for example 0.06 hrs/L.

steps.title: Only the display changes
steps.text: Saved fill-ups do not change. The dashboard, the vehicle register and the reports simply show the new unit.

guides.title: Email reports to your accountant or head office
guides.blurb: Allow an outside email domain for scheduled reports.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Allow their domain
steps.text: Scheduled reports can always go to your own users. To send them to an outside company, type its email domain here, for example accountants.co.za. Separate several domains with commas, then click Save next to the box.

steps.title: Then schedule the report
steps.text: Next, set up the report under Reports > Scheduled Mailers. The guide Email a report automatically walks you through it.

guides.title: Make clients sign for every delivery
guides.blurb: Require signatures, and a photo of the signed delivery note.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Client signature
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory Client Signature. The person receiving the goods must then sign on the driver's phone before the stop can be saved.

steps.title: Driver signature
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory Driver Signature if the driver must sign the ePOD as well.

steps.title: Paper delivery note
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory POD Photo if your clients also sign a paper delivery note. The driver must then photograph it.

guides.title: Record damaged and short deliveries properly
guides.blurb: Require photos of the goods and of damage, and decide whether drivers may deliver less than planned.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Photo of the goods
steps.text: Switch on Mandatory Evidence Photo so the driver must photograph the goods at every stop.

steps.title: Damaged goods
steps.text: Switch on Damaged Goods Need A Photo. A line marked Damaged then needs a note and a photo before the stop can be saved.

steps.title: Short deliveries
steps.text: Switch on Allow Partial Deliveries if drivers may hand over less than planned. The stop is then saved as Partial and waits under Deliveries > Resolve.

guides.title: Let drivers add stops and choose their truck
guides.blurb: Allow unplanned stops, and decide how the vehicle on the ePOD is chosen.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Unplanned stops
steps.text: Switch on Allow Unplanned Stops if drivers may capture a delivery or collection the office never loaded. Leave it off if every stop must be planned first.

steps.title: Which vehicle goes on the ePOD
steps.text: Ask the driver once per shift suits drivers who keep one truck all day. Ask on every stop suits drivers who swap vehicles. Use the vehicle the office assigned takes the vehicle from the planned delivery.

steps.title: Default loading point
steps.text: Type where goods are usually loaded, for example the main warehouse. It is printed on ePODs that have no loading point of their own.

guides.title: Email ePODs to clients automatically
guides.blurb: Send the ePOD as soon as a stop syncs, copy the office, and choose what is on it.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Open Settings in the menu on the left.

steps.title: Send it automatically
steps.text: Switch on Email The ePOD Automatically. Each client then gets the PDF as soon as the driver's stop syncs. Leave it off to send ePODs by hand from Deliveries.

steps.title: Copy the office
steps.text: Type an office address, for example pod@yourcompany.co.za, to get a copy of every ePOD email.

steps.title: Clients who opted out
steps.text: Some clients are set to Do not email ePODs. Switch on Office Copy For Opted-Out Clients if the office should still get their ePODs.

steps.title: What is on the ePOD
steps.text: Photos On The ePOD adds the delivery photos on a page after the signatures. ePOD For Failed Stops also makes a PDF when a stop could not be completed.
